title: Decision-frame extractors for region/tier fallback debugging
creator: Diego Ramirez
description:
Problem: When a request traverses the smart routing layer it may be rerouted across regions, tiers, or to fallback model variants. Current logs capture a final decision and coarse trace spans but we cannot efficiently reconstruct the per-decision signal chain for debugging noisy latency regressions or cost spikes.

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'decision-frame' extractor that emits stitchable, time-ordered micro-frames for each routing hop and policy evaluation. Each frame should be compact (<= 1KB typical), indexable by request_id, and include: timestamp, decision_id, evaluator, inputs (hash/prefix), score/priority, selected_target (region/tier/model_variant), reason_code, cost_estimate_delta, and sampling_flag. Frames will be consumable by downstream rollup pipelines and the Console's decision inspector.

Scope & approach:
- Add an instrumentation layer in the routing service that emits micro-frames synchronously to a low-cost append store (Kafka topic: routing.frames.compact) with adaptive sampling and compression.
- Implement a postprocessor that groups frames into an event bundle and computes derived metrics: hop latency, decision queue delay, cumulative cost delta, and variant-fallback chain.
- Expose a debug API that returns a short (base64) compressed bundle for a request_id for fast retrieval by SRE/Support.

Trade-offs considered:
- Synchronous vs asynchronous emission: choose synchronous best-effort write for first-hop frames to avoid losing critical initial decision context; subsequent hops can be buffered. This balances fidelity vs immediate latency impact.
- Sampling policy: default 1% system-wide, 100% for requests flagged by alerts (high latency, error rate), and 10% for canary tenants. Sampling metadata is included in the frame to allow unbiased rollups.
- Retention sizing: frames are compact to limit storage; long-term retention for aggregated rollups only (30d raw frames, 365d rollups).

Success criteria:
- Console inspector can reconstruct a route chain for 95% of sampled failing requests within 500ms of query.
- End-to-end storage costs for frames stay under 2% of overall telemetry budget in perf tests.
- Engineers can locally replay decision chains and reproduce a failing fallback within the dev environment using the bundled frames and routing-sim tool.
comments: 2026-03-10 Diego Ramirez: initial spike findings attached. Recorded that region-selection evaluators frequently add 120-200us in p95 under medium load; KV cache misses trigger extra policy checks. Pushed prototype extractor to feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pulls/4321.

2026-03-11 Priya Kapoor: reviewed proto schema. Suggested removing full prompt text and using a 64-bit hash + prefix for privacy and size. Also requested an explicit "reason_code" enum to unify fallback rationales between runtime and console. Added labels for sampling and cost metrics.

2026-03-11 Diego Ramirez: updated emitter to include sampling_flag and cost_estimate_delta. Implemented synchronous best-effort writes for the policy layer (first frame) and batched async writes for subsequent frames. Perf microbenchmark: end-to-end p50 added 22us, p99 added 210us (under test harness). Details: https://confluence.redwood/ROUTING/decision-frames-spike.

2026-03-12 SRE review (Marta Klein): confirmed kafka topic config and retention. Raised a concern about peak write amplification during traffic spikes; recommended backpressure fallback to local ring buffer with drop-on-overflow and a dropped_counter metric. Action: add drop metric + alert threshold.

2026-03-12 Diego Ramirez: implemented ring buffer fallback and dropped_counter with an initial alert at 0.1% of incoming requests. Updated unit tests and integration tests. PR updated: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pulls/4387.

2026-03-13 Product feedback (Samir Patel): Console UX needs a preview mode that shows the compact bundle decoded inline and a 'reconstruct chain' button. Logged follow-up PM ticket to design the inspector interactions. Link: https://drive.redwood/console/inspector-designs/v1.pdf.

2026-03-13 Priya Kapoor: running e2e test against staging. Observed one case where fallback model variant selection lacked a reason_code (edge case for preemptive quota). Added coverage and plan to run a 24h smoke run on staging tomorrow.
notes: Implementation details: the frame schema is intentionally minimal. Example compact frame (base64 payload when decoded): \ntimestamp=2026-03-11T18:21:34.123Z;req=abcd1234;dec=DF-0001;eval=latency_predictor;ihash=0x7fa3;score=0.82;target=us-west-2:prod-high;reason=capacity_fence;cost_delta=0.003;sf=1\nWe will iterate on enum naming for reason and add mapping to Console. Ensure consumer idempotency and graceful handling of out-of-order frames.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: instrument routing service and emit frames to kafka topic; add ring buffer fallback and metrics (2 weeks). Phase 2: postprocessor + rollup job + Console inspector integration (3 weeks). Phase 3: traffic ramp and cost tuning + archived rollup storage (2 weeks).
qa_plan: Unit tests for emitter/backpressure, integration tests with Kafka local cluster, staging 24h smoke test with fault injection for region outage simulation, and a SLO verification run comparing pre/post CPU and p99 latency impact.
deployment_playbook:
- Deploy emitter toggle behind feature flag.
- Enable 0.1% sampling in prod initially.
- Watch dropped_counter, topic_lag, and routing-inspector API latency.
- If dropped_counter > 0.5% for 30m, rollback toggle.
- After 72h stable, increase sample to 1% and enable Console inspector read path.
blocking_issues: Need final enum list for reason_code from Policy team (owner: Policy Service)
